question: Do word caps cause distillation (facts kept, words cut) or truncation (facts lost/mangled)?
method: One fixed task (document `comments gate` exit-code logic from pkg/comment/gate.go). Golden list of 10 facts extracted from source. Three writer conditions, capped writers produce draft1 + one quality-rewrite iteration. Fresh-context judge scores each fact covered/absent/mangled per draft.

fixture.task: How does `comments gate` decide its exit code?

findings: Zero truncation artifacts in any condition: under-cap omission was editorial (peripheral facts dropped whole), never mid-fact chopping.
A cap near the content's true information load (120w for 10 facts) reached full coverage at ~1/6 the uncapped length.
An over-tight cap (40w) cost coverage (7/10) but degraded gracefully: core decision logic kept, peripheral facts cleanly omitted.
Self-rewrite iteration polished wording but never recovered omitted facts (7->7, 10->10); only an external reviewer naming omissions can.
Uncapped baseline earned nothing over cap-120w on fact coverage; its extra 500 words were additive detail a reviewer must read anyway.

rubric_judging.method: Two independent fresh-context judges, NO fact checklist: each reads gate.go itself, scores accuracy/completeness/clarity/review-efficiency 1-5, ranks drafts for the purpose 'docs a human will review'. Draft order shuffled between judges.
rubric_judging.agreement: Identical tiering: both judges place the two cap-120 drafts and uncapped in the top 3 and both cap-40 drafts last (iterated above draft1). Disagreement only on ordering within the top tier.
rubric_judging.accuracy: All five drafts scored 5/5 accuracy by both judges; zero factual errors found.
judge_discoveries_beyond_golden_list: Template structural violations ALSO flip the gate to exit 10 at the CLI layer (cmd/comments/gate.go:89-101) — missed by the 10-fact golden list; no draft mentions it.
A suggestion marked Blocking never blocks in normal mode (gate.go:43 continue diverts it to pending-suggestions before the Blocking check).
Only the uncapped draft states that recorded signoffs play no role in the gate computation — judge1 called this a real reader trap in the shorter drafts.
rubric_judging.review_efficiency: Both judges scored uncapped LOWEST on value-per-minute (3/5); cap-120 drafts highest.

cap_sweep.method: Same fixture, caps forced far below the ~96-word information load: 25/15/8/3 words, two independent writers per cap, single-shot (no iteration), checklist-judged.
cap_sweep.survival_order: F3 (blocking->exit10) survives to 3 words in BOTH independent runs; then F2 (pass condition) to 15; F4/F6/F7 via qualifier entailment to 8-15; F5 (strict scope) degrades rather than dies — mangled at 15 and 8; F1 labels die below 25; F8-F10 absent at every cap in this sweep.
findings: Prioritization is consistent, not random: both 3-word runs independently kept the same fact, and it is the right one (the core failure trigger).

Truncation artifacts exist and were finally observed — but their form is DROPPED QUALIFIERS that silently narrow scope (strict mode losing its pending-suggestion arm), not visible fragments. The output stays fluent while becoming wrong-ish.
The danger zone is the MIDDLE: caps at roughly 1/6 to 1/12 of the information load (15w, 8w here) produced confident ambiguity; absurd caps (3w) degraded gracefully back to a single true fact.

Template implication: a cap at or above the section's information load is free (main pilot); a cap slightly below breeds fluent semantic corruption a reviewer may not catch; if forced to choose, far-too-tight is safer than slightly-too-tight.

multi_round_edit.method: Round 1: the 104w/10-fact doc (cap 120). Round 2: three NEW facts injected as reviewer comments (the rubric judges' discoveries: template-violation gating, blocking-suggestion diversion, signoffs-ignored); golden list grows to 13 (~125w load vs 120w cap). Two paths, two runs each: EDIT the existing doc vs FRESH rewrite from source with same scope. Round 3: edited docs compacted to 80w. All judged against the 13-fact list.
findings: EDIT beat FRESH decisively: both edits absorbed all 3 new facts while keeping all 10 originals (13/13); both fresh rewrites lost originals 8-10, MANGLED fact 10 into its opposite (missing sidecar rendered as an error), and one busted the cap.

Mechanism: the existing capped doc is compressed memory of prior editorial decisions; editing preserves that state, rewriting from source re-rolls prioritization and spends budget on ungoldened material (exit codes 1/2).
This refines rewrite-not-expand: REWRITE THE PROSE, KEEP THE DOC — restructure within the artifact; never regenerate from source once an artifact has survived review.

80w compaction of the curated doc: 12/13, zero mangles — far gentler than the sweep's fresh-writes at similar load ratios. Compacting distilled text degrades more gracefully than generating fresh at a tight cap; qualifier erosion (dropped 'structural', dropped attribution) is the leading edge of loss.
The one fact sacrificed by both compactions was the same (F8, commented-is-reply-pass) — prioritization under pressure stayed consistent across runs, as in the sweep.

saturation.method: Cap held at 80w while facts injected across rounds: round 4 adds facts 14-16 (load ~150w, 1.9x cap), round 5 adds 17-19 (load ~180w, 2.25x cap). Two independent edit chains continuing from the round-3 compacted docs. Judged against the 19-fact list tagged by injection round.
findings: No collapse at 2.25x overload: 16-17/19 facts held in ~78 words with zero mangles at round 5 — the doc behaves like an importance-ranked cache, not a corrupting buffer.

Eviction is IMPORTANCE-based, not recency-based — with one bias: the newest injection always arrives intact (reviewer comments are salient), so the squeeze falls on MID-AGE NUANCE. Both chains evicted round-2 subtleties (blocking-suggestion diversion; one chain also signoff-irrelevance) to seat round-5 facts.
Evictions are SILENT: nothing in the edit output announces that a previously-covered fact fell out; only a fact-list diff catches it. In the real loop no reviewer would notice.
Continued editing can REPAIR degradation: chain B's round-4 mangle of fact 11 (enforcement locus ambiguity) came back clean in round 5.

Workflow implication (the eval's actionable output): when a capped doc saturates, require the agent to DECLARE evictions in its reply ('dropped X to seat Y') — turning silent cache eviction into a reviewable decision. Candidate skill/template rule.

citation_overhead.method: Cap 120w, fresh writes covering all 19 facts' scope; CIT condition requires a file:line citation per claim (citations count toward cap), UNCIT has no citation requirement. Two runs each, judged against the 19-fact list.
findings: Citations consumed 11-12% of the budget (~13-14 words) and cost about ONE fact at this cap (CIT avg 12.5 vs UNCIT 13.5) — real but modest. Caveat: the best uncited run was also 3 words over cap.
The shared fact-18 mangle (check_citations conditionality flattened to always-on) appeared identically in citation-free drafts — a compression failure mode, not a citation cost.

Template action: exclude citation tokens (file:line refs) from word-cap counting in validate, so citing is never taxed against content — aligns the incentive with the plan template's cite-everything rule.

sentence_caps.method: Cap 80w (overloaded: 19-fact scope), SHORT condition adds 'every sentence <=15 words', FREE has no sentence limit. Two runs each, judged with attention to compound-qualifier facts (5, 11, 18).
findings: The sentence cap did NOT hurt coverage (slightly helped) and produced ZERO mangles vs two in free-sentence runs.

Failure-mode asymmetry: short sentences OMIT tight qualifiers wholesale (absent — visible, safer); free sentences squeeze qualifiers in and BREAK them (mangled — invisible, misleads). Absence beats corruption for review purposes.
One split-but-survived case: a dropped qualifier in one bullet was repaired by the adjacent bullet — short-sentence redundancy self-corrects.
Template action: KEEP the max_sentence_words style rule; no relaxation needed for invariant-heavy sections — the rule is protective, not just cosmetic.

caveats: Single task, single run per condition in the main pilot (two per cap in the sweep and multi-round), writer and judges share a model family. Checklist judge flagged fact 7's 'tracked separately' clause as the softest scoring call. One rubric-judge run lost to an API disconnect and rerun.
artifacts: golden facts + drafts in session scratchpad cap-eval/ (ephemeral); this log is the durable record
